text: Sales schema table REGIONS(REGION_ID NUMBER PK, REGION_NAME VARCHAR2, COUNTRY VARCHAR2). Lookup table of sales regions and their countries.

Sales schema table CUSTOMERS(CUSTOMER_ID NUMBER PK, FIRST_NAME VARCHAR2, LAST_NAME VARCHAR2, EMAIL VARCHAR2, REGION_ID NUMBER FK->REGIONS, SIGNUP_DATE DATE, CUSTOMER_TIER VARCHAR2 ['STANDARD','SILVER','GOLD','PLATINUM']). Customer master data.
Sales schema table PRODUCTS(PRODUCT_ID NUMBER PK, PRODUCT_NAME VARCHAR2, CATEGORY VARCHAR2, UNIT_PRICE NUMBER, STOCK_QTY NUMBER). Product catalog with pricing and inventory.

Sales schema table ORDERS(ORDER_ID NUMBER PK, CUSTOMER_ID NUMBER FK->CUSTOMERS, ORDER_DATE DATE, STATUS VARCHAR2 ['PENDING','COMPLETED','CANCELLED','REFUNDED'], REGION_ID NUMBER FK->REGIONS). Order header records.

Sales schema table ORDER_ITEMS(ORDER_ITEM_ID NUMBER PK, ORDER_ID NUMBER FK->ORDERS, PRODUCT_ID NUMBER FK->PRODUCTS, QUANTITY NUMBER, UNIT_PRICE NUMBER). Line items per order; used for revenue calculations (QUANTITY * UNIT_PRICE).
HR schema table HR_LOCATIONS(LOCATION_ID NUMBER PK, CITY VARCHAR2, COUNTRY VARCHAR2). Physical office locations.
HR schema table HR_DEPARTMENTS(DEPARTMENT_ID NUMBER PK, DEPARTMENT_NAME VARCHAR2, LOCATION_ID NUMBER FK->HR_LOCATIONS). Company departments.
HR schema table HR_JOBS(JOB_ID NUMBER PK, JOB_TITLE VARCHAR2, MIN_SALARY NUMBER, MAX_SALARY NUMBER). Job title catalog with salary bands.

HR schema table HR_EMPLOYEES(EMPLOYEE_ID NUMBER PK, FIRST_NAME VARCHAR2, LAST_NAME VARCHAR2, EMAIL VARCHAR2, HIRE_DATE DATE, JOB_ID NUMBER FK->HR_JOBS, SALARY NUMBER, DEPARTMENT_ID NUMBER FK->HR_DEPARTMENTS, MANAGER_ID NUMBER FK->HR_EMPLOYEES self-referencing). Employee master data with self-referencing manager hierarchy.

HR schema table HR_JOB_HISTORY(EMPLOYEE_ID NUMBER FK->HR_EMPLOYEES, START_DATE DATE, END_DATE DATE nullable, JOB_ID NUMBER FK->HR_JOBS, DEPARTMENT_ID NUMBER FK->HR_DEPARTMENTS, PK(EMPLOYEE_ID, START_DATE)). Historical record of past roles/departments per employee.

Example question: List all products in the 'Electronics' category.
SQL: SELECT * FROM PRODUCTS WHERE CATEGORY = 'Electronics' ORDER BY PRODUCT_ID

Example question: Show all customers in the 'GOLD' tier.
SQL: SELECT * FROM CUSTOMERS WHERE CUSTOMER_TIER = 'GOLD' ORDER BY CUSTOMER_ID

Example question: Find products with a unit price greater than 500.
SQL: SELECT * FROM PRODUCTS WHERE UNIT_PRICE > 500 ORDER BY PRODUCT_ID

Example question: List the top 10 most expensive products.
SQL: SELECT * FROM PRODUCTS ORDER BY UNIT_PRICE DESC, PRODUCT_ID FETCH FIRST 10 ROWS ONLY

Example question: Show all orders with status 'CANCELLED'.
SQL: SELECT * FROM ORDERS WHERE STATUS = 'CANCELLED' ORDER BY ORDER_ID

Example question: List customers who signed up in 2024.
SQL: SELECT * FROM CUSTOMERS WHERE SIGNUP_DATE BETWEEN DATE '2024-01-01' AND DATE '2024-12-31' ORDER BY CUSTOMER_ID

Example question: Find all regions in 'Europe'.
SQL: SELECT * FROM REGIONS WHERE REGION_NAME = 'Europe' ORDER BY REGION_ID

Example question: List products with stock quantity less than 50, ordered by stock ascending.
SQL: SELECT * FROM PRODUCTS WHERE STOCK_QTY < 50 ORDER BY STOCK_QTY, PRODUCT_ID

Example question: Show customers whose last name starts with 'A'.
SQL: SELECT * FROM CUSTOMERS WHERE LAST_NAME LIKE 'A%' ORDER BY CUSTOMER_ID

Example question: List the 5 most recent orders.
SQL: SELECT * FROM ORDERS ORDER BY ORDER_DATE DESC, ORDER_ID DESC FETCH FIRST 5 ROWS ONLY

Example question: Find all PLATINUM tier customers, ordered by signup date.
SQL: SELECT * FROM CUSTOMERS WHERE CUSTOMER_TIER = 'PLATINUM' ORDER BY SIGNUP_DATE, CUSTOMER_ID

Example question: List products in the 'Books' category with price under 20.
SQL: SELECT * FROM PRODUCTS WHERE CATEGORY = 'Books' AND UNIT_PRICE < 20 ORDER BY PRODUCT_ID

Example question: For each region, show the total number of customers.
SQL: SELECT r.REGION_NAME, COUNT(c.CUSTOMER_ID) AS customer_count
       FROM REGIONS r LEFT JOIN CUSTOMERS c ON c.REGION_ID = r.REGION_ID
       GROUP BY r.REGION_NAME ORDER BY r.REGION_NAME

Example question: Show total revenue (quantity times unit price) per product category.
SQL: SELECT p.CATEGORY, SUM(oi.QUANTITY * oi.UNIT_PRICE) AS total_revenue
       FROM ORDER_ITEMS oi JOIN PRODUCTS p ON oi.PRODUCT_ID = p.PRODUCT_ID
       GROUP BY p.CATEGORY ORDER BY p.CATEGORY

Example question: List the top 5 customers by total number of orders.
SQL: SELECT c.CUSTOMER_ID, c.LAST_NAME, COUNT(o.ORDER_ID) AS order_count
       FROM CUSTOMERS c JOIN ORDERS o ON o.CUSTOMER_ID = c.CUSTOMER_ID
       GROUP BY c.CUSTOMER_ID, c.LAST_NAME
       ORDER BY order_count DESC, c.CUSTOMER_ID FETCH FIRST 5 ROWS ONLY

Example question: For each order status, show the count of orders.
SQL: SELECT STATUS, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM ORDERS GROUP BY STATUS ORDER BY STATUS

Example question: Show the number of orders placed by customers in each customer tier.
SQL: SELECT c.CUSTOMER_TIER, COUNT(o.ORDER_ID) AS order_count
       FROM CUSTOMERS c JOIN ORDERS o ON o.CUSTOMER_ID = c.CUSTOMER_ID
       GROUP BY c.CUSTOMER_TIER ORDER BY c.CUSTOMER_TIER

Example question: List products that have never been ordered.
SQL: SELECT p.PRODUCT_ID, p.PRODUCT_NAME
       FROM PRODUCTS p LEFT JOIN ORDER_ITEMS oi ON oi.PRODUCT_ID = p.PRODUCT_ID
       WHERE oi.ORDER_ITEM_ID IS NULL ORDER BY p.PRODUCT_ID

Example question: Show total quantity sold per product, only for products with total quantity greater than 1000.
SQL: SELECT p.PRODUCT_ID, p.PRODUCT_NAME, SUM(oi.QUANTITY) AS total_qty
       FROM PRODUCTS p JOIN ORDER_ITEMS oi ON oi.PRODUCT_ID = p.PRODUCT_ID
       GROUP BY p.PRODUCT_ID, p.PRODUCT_NAME
       HAVING SUM(oi.QUANTITY) > 1000 ORDER BY p.PRODUCT_ID

Example question: For each region, calculate total order revenue in that region.
SQL: SELECT r.REGION_NAME, SUM(oi.QUANTITY * oi.UNIT_PRICE) AS total_revenue
       FROM REGIONS r JOIN ORDERS o ON o.REGION_ID = r.REGION_ID
       JOIN ORDER_ITEMS oi ON oi.ORDER_ID = o.ORDER_ID
       GROUP BY r.REGION_NAME ORDER BY r.REGION_NAME

Example question: List the number of orders per month for the year 2025.
SQL: SELECT EXTRACT(MONTH FROM ORDER_DATE) AS order_month, COUNT(*) AS order_count
       FROM ORDERS WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM ORDER_DATE) = 2025
       GROUP BY EXTRACT(MONTH FROM ORDER_DATE) ORDER BY order_month

Example question: Show each customer's total spend, only for customers who spent more than 5000.
SQL: SELECT c.CUSTOMER_ID, c.LAST_NAME, SUM(oi.QUANTITY * oi.UNIT_PRICE) AS total_spend
       FROM CUSTOMERS c JOIN ORDERS o ON o.CUSTOMER_ID = c.CUSTOMER_ID
       JOIN ORDER_ITEMS oi ON oi.ORDER_ID = o.ORDER_ID
       GROUP BY c.CUSTOMER_ID, c.LAST_NAME
       HAVING SUM(oi.QUANTITY * oi.UNIT_PRICE) > 5000 ORDER BY c.CUSTOMER_ID

Example question: List the average unit price of products per category, ordered descending by average price.
SQL: SELECT CATEGORY, AVG(UNIT_PRICE) AS avg_price
       FROM PRODUCTS GROUP BY CATEGORY ORDER BY avg_price DESC, CATEGORY

Example question: For each product, show how many distinct customers have purchased it.
SQL: SELECT p.PRODUCT_ID, p.PRODUCT_NAME, COUNT(DISTINCT o.CUSTOMER_ID) AS distinct_customers
       FROM PRODUCTS p JOIN ORDER_ITEMS oi ON oi.PRODUCT_ID = p.PRODUCT_ID
       JOIN ORDERS o ON o.ORDER_ID = oi.ORDER_ID
       GROUP BY p.PRODUCT_ID, p.PRODUCT_NAME ORDER BY p.PRODUCT_ID

Example question: Rank customers by total spend within each region using a window function.
SQL: SELECT * FROM (
         SELECT c.CUSTOMER_ID, c.LAST_NAME, r.REGION_NAME,
                SUM(oi.QUANTITY * oi.UNIT_PRICE) AS total_spend,
                RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY r.REGION_NAME ORDER BY SUM(oi.QUANTITY * oi.UNIT_PRICE) DESC) AS spend_rank
         FROM CUSTOMERS c JOIN REGIONS r ON c.REGION_ID = r.REGION_ID
         JOIN ORDERS o ON o.CUSTOMER_ID = c.CUSTOMER_ID
         JOIN ORDER_ITEMS oi ON oi.ORDER_ID = o.ORDER_ID
         GROUP BY c.CUSTOMER_ID, c.LAST_NAME, r.REGION_NAME
       ) WHERE spend_rank <= 3 ORDER BY REGION_NAME, spend_rank

Example question: Show products whose price is above the average price of their own category.
SQL: SELECT p.PRODUCT_ID, p.PRODUCT_NAME, p.CATEGORY, p.UNIT_PRICE
       FROM PRODUCTS p
       WHERE p.UNIT_PRICE > (SELECT AVG(p2.UNIT_PRICE) FROM PRODUCTS p2 WHERE p2.CATEGORY = p.CATEGORY)
       ORDER BY p.PRODUCT_ID

Example question: List the top 3 highest-priced products per category using a window function.
SQL: SELECT * FROM (
         SELECT PRODUCT_ID, PRODUCT_NAME, CATEGORY, UNIT_PRICE,
                ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY CATEGORY ORDER BY UNIT_PRICE DESC, PRODUCT_ID) AS rn
         FROM PRODUCTS
       ) WHERE rn <= 3 ORDER BY CATEGORY, rn

Example question: For each customer, show their most recent order date and a running total of their order count over time.
SQL: SELECT CUSTOMER_ID, ORDER_ID, ORDER_DATE,
              COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY CUSTOMER_ID ORDER BY ORDER_DATE, ORDER_ID
                             ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_order_count
       FROM ORDERS WHERE CUSTOMER_ID <= 10
       ORDER BY CUSTOMER_ID, ORDER_DATE, ORDER_ID

Example question: List customers who have placed more orders than the average number of orders per customer.
SQL: SELECT c.CUSTOMER_ID, c.LAST_NAME, COUNT(o.ORDER_ID) AS order_count
       FROM CUSTOMERS c JOIN ORDERS o ON o.CUSTOMER_ID = c.CUSTOMER_ID
       GROUP BY c.CUSTOMER_ID, c.LAST_NAME
       HAVING COUNT(o.ORDER_ID) > (
         SELECT AVG(cnt) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM ORDERS GROUP BY CUSTOMER_ID)
       )
       ORDER BY c.CUSTOMER_ID

Example question: Increase stock quantity by 10 for all products in the 'Toys' category using a MERGE statement, then show the affected products.
SQL: MERGE INTO PRODUCTS p
       USING (SELECT PRODUCT_ID FROM PRODUCTS WHERE CATEGORY = 'Toys') src
       ON (p.PRODUCT_ID = src.PRODUCT_ID)
       WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET p.STOCK_QTY = p.STOCK_QTY + 10

Example question: Find the second highest-priced product in each category using a window function.
SQL: SELECT * FROM (
         SELECT PRODUCT_ID, PRODUCT_NAME, CATEGORY, UNIT_PRICE,
                DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY CATEGORY ORDER BY UNIT_PRICE DESC) AS rnk
         FROM PRODUCTS
       ) WHERE rnk = 2 ORDER BY CATEGORY

Example question: Show month-over-month revenue and the percentage change from the previous month for 2025, using LAG().
SQL: SELECT order_month, monthly_revenue,
              ROUND((monthly_revenue - LAG(monthly_revenue) OVER (ORDER BY order_month))
                    / LAG(monthly_revenue) OVER (ORDER BY order_month) * 100, 2) AS pct_change
       FROM (
         SELECT EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.ORDER_DATE) AS order_month,
                SUM(oi.QUANTITY * oi.UNIT_PRICE) AS monthly_revenue
         FROM ORDERS o JOIN ORDER_ITEMS oi ON oi.ORDER_ID = o.ORDER_ID
         WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.ORDER_DATE) = 2025
         GROUP BY EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.ORDER_DATE)
       ) ORDER BY order_month

Example question: Compute a 3-month moving average of order counts using a window function.
SQL: SELECT order_month, order_count,
              ROUND(AVG(order_count) OVER (ORDER BY order_month ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW), 2) AS moving_avg
       FROM (
         SELECT TRUNC(ORDER_DATE, 'MM') AS order_month, COUNT(*) AS order_count
         FROM ORDERS GROUP BY TRUNC(ORDER_DATE, 'MM')
       ) ORDER BY order_month

Example question: List the top 3 customers by total spend in each region using a window function.
SQL: SELECT * FROM (
         SELECT c.CUSTOMER_ID, c.LAST_NAME, r.REGION_NAME,
                SUM(oi.QUANTITY * oi.UNIT_PRICE) AS total_spend,
                ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY r.REGION_NAME ORDER BY SUM(oi.QUANTITY * oi.UNIT_PRICE) DESC) AS rn
         FROM CUSTOMERS c JOIN REGIONS r ON c.REGION_ID = r.REGION_ID
         JOIN ORDERS o ON o.CUSTOMER_ID = c.CUSTOMER_ID
         JOIN ORDER_ITEMS oi ON oi.ORDER_ID = o.ORDER_ID
         GROUP BY c.CUSTOMER_ID, c.LAST_NAME, r.REGION_NAME
       ) WHERE rn <= 3 ORDER BY REGION_NAME, rn

Example question: Find products that are priced higher than all products in the 'Garden' category.
SQL: SELECT PRODUCT_ID, PRODUCT_NAME, CATEGORY, UNIT_PRICE
       FROM PRODUCTS
       WHERE UNIT_PRICE > ALL (SELECT UNIT_PRICE FROM PRODUCTS WHERE CATEGORY = 'Garden')
       ORDER BY PRODUCT_ID

Example question: Show cumulative revenue per day for January 2025, ordered by date, using a running total.
SQL: SELECT order_day, daily_revenue,
              SUM(daily_revenue) OVER (ORDER BY order_day ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS cumulative_revenue
       FROM (
         SELECT TRUNC(o.ORDER_DATE) AS order_day, SUM(oi.QUANTITY * oi.UNIT_PRICE) AS daily_revenue
         FROM ORDERS o JOIN ORDER_ITEMS oi ON oi.ORDER_ID = o.ORDER_ID
         WHERE o.ORDER_DATE >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND o.ORDER_DATE < DATE '2025-02-01'
         GROUP BY TRUNC(o.ORDER_DATE)
       ) ORDER BY order_day

Example question: List employees hired after January 1, 2023.
SQL: SELECT * FROM HR_EMPLOYEES WHERE HIRE_DATE > DATE '2023-01-01' ORDER BY EMPLOYEE_ID

Example question: Show employees with salary greater than 150000.
SQL: SELECT * FROM HR_EMPLOYEES WHERE SALARY > 150000 ORDER BY EMPLOYEE_ID

Example question: List all job titles with a max salary above 200000.
SQL: SELECT * FROM HR_JOBS WHERE MAX_SALARY > 200000 ORDER BY JOB_ID

Example question: Show the top 10 highest paid employees.
SQL: SELECT * FROM HR_EMPLOYEES ORDER BY SALARY DESC, EMPLOYEE_ID FETCH FIRST 10 ROWS ONLY

Example question: List all locations in the USA.
SQL: SELECT * FROM HR_LOCATIONS WHERE COUNTRY = 'USA' ORDER BY LOCATION_ID

Example question: Find employees whose last name contains 'son'.
SQL: SELECT * FROM HR_EMPLOYEES WHERE LAST_NAME LIKE '%son%' ORDER BY EMPLOYEE_ID

Example question: List all department names.
SQL: SELECT DEPARTMENT_NAME FROM HR_DEPARTMENTS ORDER BY DEPARTMENT_ID

Example question: Show employees hired in 2020, ordered by hire date.
SQL: SELECT * FROM HR_EMPLOYEES WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM HIRE_DATE) = 2020 ORDER BY HIRE_DATE, EMPLOYEE_ID

Example question: List the 5 most recently hired employees.
SQL: SELECT * FROM HR_EMPLOYEES ORDER BY HIRE_DATE DESC, EMPLOYEE_ID DESC FETCH FIRST 5 ROWS ONLY

Example question: Find all job titles containing 'Manager'.
SQL: SELECT * FROM HR_JOBS WHERE JOB_TITLE LIKE '%Manager%' ORDER BY JOB_ID

Example question: Show employees with no manager assigned (top-level employees).
SQL: SELECT * FROM HR_EMPLOYEES WHERE MANAGER_ID IS NULL ORDER BY EMPLOYEE_ID

Example question: List employees with salary between 80000 and 120000, ordered by salary.
SQL: SELECT * FROM HR_EMPLOYEES WHERE SALARY BETWEEN 80000 AND 120000 ORDER BY SALARY, EMPLOYEE_ID

Example question: For each department, show the number of employees.
SQL: SELECT d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, COUNT(e.EMPLOYEE_ID) AS emp_count
       FROM HR_DEPARTMENTS d LEFT JOIN HR_EMPLOYEES e ON e.DEPARTMENT_ID = d.DEPARTMENT_ID
       GROUP BY d.DEPARTMENT_NAME ORDER BY d.DEPARTMENT_NAME

Example question: Show average salary per job title, ordered descending by average salary.
SQL: SELECT j.JOB_TITLE, AVG(e.SALARY) AS avg_salary
       FROM HR_JOBS j JOIN HR_EMPLOYEES e ON e.JOB_ID = j.JOB_ID
       GROUP BY j.JOB_TITLE ORDER BY avg_salary DESC, j.JOB_TITLE

Example question: List departments with more than 600 employees.
SQL: SELECT d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, COUNT(e.EMPLOYEE_ID) AS emp_count
       FROM HR_DEPARTMENTS d JOIN HR_EMPLOYEES e ON e.DEPARTMENT_ID = d.DEPARTMENT_ID
       GROUP BY d.DEPARTMENT_NAME
       HAVING COUNT(e.EMPLOYEE_ID) > 600 ORDER BY d.DEPARTMENT_NAME

Example question: For each location, show the total number of departments.
SQL: SELECT l.CITY, l.COUNTRY, COUNT(d.DEPARTMENT_ID) AS dept_count
       FROM HR_LOCATIONS l LEFT JOIN HR_DEPARTMENTS d ON d.LOCATION_ID = l.LOCATION_ID
       GROUP BY l.CITY, l.COUNTRY ORDER BY l.CITY

Example question: Show the count of direct reports per manager, for the top 10 managers by team size.
SQL: SELECT m.EMPLOYEE_ID, m.LAST_NAME, COUNT(e.EMPLOYEE_ID) AS report_count
       FROM HR_EMPLOYEES m JOIN HR_EMPLOYEES e ON e.MANAGER_ID = m.EMPLOYEE_ID
       GROUP BY m.EMPLOYEE_ID, m.LAST_NAME
       ORDER BY report_count DESC, m.EMPLOYEE_ID FETCH FIRST 10 ROWS ONLY

Example question: List the total salary cost per department, ordered descending.
SQL: SELECT d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, SUM(e.SALARY) AS total_salary
       FROM HR_DEPARTMENTS d JOIN HR_EMPLOYEES e ON e.DEPARTMENT_ID = d.DEPARTMENT_ID
       GROUP BY d.DEPARTMENT_NAME ORDER BY total_salary DESC, d.DEPARTMENT_NAME

Example question: For each job title, show the minimum, maximum, and average employee salary.
SQL: SELECT j.JOB_TITLE, MIN(e.SALARY) AS min_sal, MAX(e.SALARY) AS max_sal, AVG(e.SALARY) AS avg_sal
       FROM HR_JOBS j JOIN HR_EMPLOYEES e ON e.JOB_ID = j.JOB_ID
       GROUP BY j.JOB_TITLE ORDER BY j.JOB_TITLE

Example question: Show departments where the average salary exceeds 120000.
SQL: SELECT d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, AVG(e.SALARY) AS avg_salary
       FROM HR_DEPARTMENTS d JOIN HR_EMPLOYEES e ON e.DEPARTMENT_ID = d.DEPARTMENT_ID
       GROUP BY d.DEPARTMENT_NAME
       HAVING AVG(e.SALARY) > 120000 ORDER BY d.DEPARTMENT_NAME

Example question: List the number of employees hired each year, ordered by year.
SQL: SELECT EXTRACT(YEAR FROM HIRE_DATE) AS hire_year, COUNT(*) AS emp_count
       FROM HR_EMPLOYEES GROUP BY EXTRACT(YEAR FROM HIRE_DATE) ORDER BY hire_year

Example question: For each country, show the total number of employees working there.
SQL: SELECT l.COUNTRY, COUNT(e.EMPLOYEE_ID) AS emp_count
       FROM HR_LOCATIONS l JOIN HR_DEPARTMENTS d ON d.LOCATION_ID = l.LOCATION_ID
       JOIN HR_EMPLOYEES e ON e.DEPARTMENT_ID = d.DEPARTMENT_ID
       GROUP BY l.COUNTRY ORDER BY l.COUNTRY

Example question: Show employees along with their department name and job title, limited to the 'Sales' department.
SQL: SELECT e.EMPLOYEE_ID, e.FIRST_NAME, e.LAST_NAME, d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, j.JOB_TITLE
       FROM HR_EMPLOYEES e JOIN HR_DEPARTMENTS d ON e.DEPARTMENT_ID = d.DEPARTMENT_ID
       JOIN HR_JOBS j ON e.JOB_ID = j.JOB_ID
       WHERE d.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Sales' ORDER BY e.EMPLOYEE_ID

Example question: List employees who have more than 1 job history record, along with their history count.
SQL: SELECT e.EMPLOYEE_ID, e.LAST_NAME, COUNT(jh.START_DATE) AS history_count
       FROM HR_EMPLOYEES e JOIN HR_JOB_HISTORY jh ON jh.EMPLOYEE_ID = e.EMPLOYEE_ID
       GROUP BY e.EMPLOYEE_ID, e.LAST_NAME
       HAVING COUNT(jh.START_DATE) > 1 ORDER BY e.EMPLOYEE_ID

Example question: Show the organizational hierarchy starting from the top (employees with no manager) using CONNECT BY, including hierarchy level, limited to 3 levels.
SQL: SELECT EMPLOYEE_ID, LAST_NAME, MANAGER_ID, LEVEL AS hier_level
       FROM HR_EMPLOYEES
       START WITH MANAGER_ID IS NULL
       CONNECT BY PRIOR EMPLOYEE_ID = MANAGER_ID
       AND LEVEL <= 3
       ORDER BY hier_level, EMPLOYEE_ID

Example question: Rank employees by salary within each department using RANK().
SQL: SELECT DEPARTMENT_ID, EMPLOYEE_ID, LAST_NAME, SALARY,
              RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY DEPARTMENT_ID ORDER BY SALARY DESC) AS salary_rank
       FROM HR_EMPLOYEES ORDER BY DEPARTMENT_ID, salary_rank

Example question: Find employees who earn more than their manager.
SQL: SELECT e.EMPLOYEE_ID, e.LAST_NAME, e.SALARY, m.EMPLOYEE_ID AS manager_id, m.SALARY AS manager_salary
       FROM HR_EMPLOYEES e JOIN HR_EMPLOYEES m ON e.MANAGER_ID = m.EMPLOYEE_ID
       WHERE e.SALARY > m.SALARY ORDER BY e.EMPLOYEE_ID

Example question: Show the top 3 highest paid employees per department using a window function.
SQL: SELECT * FROM (
         SELECT DEPARTMENT_ID, EMPLOYEE_ID, LAST_NAME, SALARY,
                ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY DEPARTMENT_ID ORDER BY SALARY DESC, EMPLOYEE_ID) AS rn
         FROM HR_EMPLOYEES
       ) WHERE rn <= 3 ORDER BY DEPARTMENT_ID, rn

Example question: List employees whose salary is above the average salary of their own department.
SQL: SELECT e.EMPLOYEE_ID, e.LAST_NAME, e.DEPARTMENT_ID, e.SALARY
       FROM HR_EMPLOYEES e
       WHERE e.SALARY > (SELECT AVG(e2.SALARY) FROM HR_EMPLOYEES e2 WHERE e2.DEPARTMENT_ID = e.DEPARTMENT_ID)
       ORDER BY e.EMPLOYEE_ID

Example question: Compute each employee's salary rank company-wide using DENSE_RANK(), showing the top 10.
SQL: SELECT * FROM (
         SELECT EMPLOYEE_ID, LAST_NAME, SALARY, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY SALARY DESC) AS rnk
         FROM HR_EMPLOYEES
       ) WHERE rnk <= 10 ORDER BY rnk, EMPLOYEE_ID

Example question: Show a running total of salary cost ordered by hire date, for employees hired in 2015.
SQL: SELECT EMPLOYEE_ID, HIRE_DATE, SALARY,
              SUM(SALARY) OVER (ORDER BY HIRE_DATE, EMPLOYEE_ID ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_total
       FROM HR_EMPLOYEES
       WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM HIRE_DATE) = 2015
       ORDER BY HIRE_DATE, EMPLOYEE_ID

Example question: Give a 5 percent raise to all employees in the 'Engineering' department using a MERGE statement.
SQL: MERGE INTO HR_EMPLOYEES e
       USING (SELECT emp.EMPLOYEE_ID FROM HR_EMPLOYEES emp
              JOIN HR_DEPARTMENTS d ON emp.DEPARTMENT_ID = d.DEPARTMENT_ID
              WHERE d.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Engineering') src
       ON (e.EMPLOYEE_ID = src.EMPLOYEE_ID)
       WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET e.SALARY = e.SALARY * 1.05

Example question: Find the department with the highest average salary.
SQL: SELECT DEPARTMENT_ID, AVG(SALARY) AS avg_salary
       FROM HR_EMPLOYEES GROUP BY DEPARTMENT_ID
       HAVING AVG(SALARY) >= ALL (SELECT AVG(SALARY) FROM HR_EMPLOYEES GROUP BY DEPARTMENT_ID)

Example question: Using CONNECT BY, list all employees who report directly or indirectly to employee 3600, with their hierarchy level.
SQL: SELECT EMPLOYEE_ID, LAST_NAME, MANAGER_ID, LEVEL AS hier_level
       FROM HR_EMPLOYEES
       START WITH EMPLOYEE_ID = 3600
       CONNECT BY PRIOR EMPLOYEE_ID = MANAGER_ID
       ORDER BY hier_level, EMPLOYEE_ID

Example question: Show the salary difference between each employee and the previously hired employee, ordered by hire date, using LAG().
SQL: SELECT EMPLOYEE_ID, HIRE_DATE, SALARY,
              SALARY - LAG(SALARY) OVER (ORDER BY HIRE_DATE, EMPLOYEE_ID) AS salary_diff_from_prev
       FROM HR_EMPLOYEES WHERE EMPLOYEE_ID <= 50
       ORDER BY HIRE_DATE, EMPLOYEE_ID

Example question: For employees with more than one job history record, show their most recent job title using an analytic function.
SQL: SELECT * FROM (
         SELECT jh.EMPLOYEE_ID, j.JOB_TITLE,
                ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY jh.EMPLOYEE_ID ORDER BY jh.START_DATE DESC) AS rn,
                COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY jh.EMPLOYEE_ID) AS history_count
         FROM HR_JOB_HISTORY jh JOIN HR_JOBS j ON jh.JOB_ID = j.JOB_ID
       ) WHERE rn = 1 AND history_count > 1 ORDER BY EMPLOYEE_ID
